org.portico.container

Class Container

  • java.lang.Object
    • org.portico.container.Container

  • public class Container
extends Object
    A Container represents the top-level in the Portico environment. Into a Container, a number of IDaemons (allowing background/separate tasks to be run) and a number of LRCs can be deployed.

    LRCs

    An LRC is the main message processing nerve-center of the Portico framework. Typically, an LRC will represent an individual federate. However, it can be used as a general data-gathering entity for third party plugins.

    Daemons

    The Container also houses a set of IDaemons. These components allow arbitrary behaviour to be inserted into the framework and run almost like background processes. See the javadoc for the IDaemon interface for more information.

    Plugins

    The container will locate and load Portico plugins (handler modules, daemons, etc...). It will keep this information stored and will manage any classpath management concerns.

    • Method Detail

      • killContainer

        public void killContainer()
        Shutdown all the components in the container. Currently this will only stop the contained daemons.

      • killLrcs

        public void killLrcs()
        Shutdown all the active LRCs with extreme prejudice. This is really only used by the testing framework which has to clean up all LRCs to avoid connection resource leaks at the end of each test.

      • getHandlerRegistry

        public HandlerRegistry getHandlerRegistry()
        Get a group of all the modules located in the container. If there are no modules, an empty set will be returned.

      • registerLrc
